articleTitle: An Integrated Rotary Transformer and 3-Phase Dual-Active-Bridge Converter for High Power Transfer in Novel X-Rotor Wind Turbines
abstract: The slip ring solution for power transfer between rotating structures has adverse impacts on the maintenance of offshore wind turbines. Rotary transformer systems transfer electric energy based on the electromagnetic induction through the air-gap without mechanical contact. The rotary transformer can be integrated into dual active bridge converters (DAB) to utilize leakage inductance instead of the cumbersome inductor used typically in the system. The X-rotor wind turbine concept uses this idea to eliminate the need for slip rings and transfer bulk power to the AC network from generators mounted in a rotating structure. In this paper the design, performance, efficiency, and manufacturing details of a 1 MW wireless power transfer system for the novel X-rotor offshore wind turbine concept is presented. The results show that this design methodology that includes rotary transformers and dual active bridge converters is suitable for high-efficiency high-power wireless transfer systems.

articleTitle: Preparation and Characterization of High Aspect Ratio Electrodeposited CoPt Multilayered Magnetic Nanowires
abstract: High aspect ratio CoPt multilayered alloy nanowires were prepared by low-cost electrodeposition technique utilizing polycarbonate template membrane (PT). The nanoholes with a 100 nm diameter of the PT were filled with CoPt multilayered alloy to generate nanowires while the potential was varied to modulate the composition of CoPt alloy. The obtained CoPt multilayered nanowires had a bamboo-like periodic structure with a relative chemical composition of [Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">80</inf>Pt<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</inf>/Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">30</inf>Pt<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">70</inf>]n. Magnetic and structural properties of multilayered nanowires have been evaluated. A single Co-rich alloy (relative composition of Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">80</inf>Pt<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</inf>) nanowire was also fabricated and exhibited ferromagnetic properties. The CoPt multilayered nanowires demonstrated improvement in magnetic anisotropy compared to the single-layered Co-rich alloy nanowires. The developed technique and multilayered nanowires can be used for emerging three-dimensional magnetic domain wall memory.

articleTitle: High Gradient Magnetic Separator Design with Hybrid Poles and Increased Efficiency
abstract: In this article, we analyze the efficiency of high gradient magnetic separator (HGMS) designs in terms of efficient use of magnetic energy. Combining analytical analysis and Boundary Element Analysis software, we evaluate the characteristics of quadrupole design, specifically, the magnetic field limits, the energy and gradient distribution, and the design efficiency. To increase the design efficiency, we present a high gradient magnetic separator (HGMS) design with partial soft magnetic steel pole pieces. The use of nearly saturated soft magnetic pole pieces increases the magnetic field in the region of interest. And the use of pole pieces also increases the efficiency of the design. Magnetic separators with and without pole piece are built to evaluate the effectiveness of the pole piece.

articleTitle: Recycling and Enrichment of Rare Earth Based Permanent Magnet Scraps
abstract: The trade dominance of China in the rare earth industry, 33.8% reserves, and 70% of the production of rare earths jeopardize the continuity of strategic applications with high-added value. Another and more important problem is that the mining of rare-earth elements is harmful to the environment. A considerable amount of rare-earth elements could be recycled back to the industry with the right recycling procedure while protecting the environment and providing economic benefits. In this work, using powder metallurgy methods, the rare-earth-based permanent magnet-containing devices currently in scrap yards were recycled. Recycling ferro magnets materials such as iron, strontium hexaferrite (SrFe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</inf>), and Neodymium Iron Boron (Nd-Fe-B) attract the attention of the industry. The rich source of SrFe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</inf> and Nd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</inf>B in scrap yards are electric motors and hard disks, respectively. Separated SrFe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</inf> and Nd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</inf>B magnets were cleaned, crushed, pulverized, recompacted, and magnetized. This study aims to reach 100% density recycled permanent magnets with magnetic properties comparable to commercial counterparts.

articleTitle: Design and Evaluation of a Linear Permanent Magnet Flux Switching Machine for Use in Dry Gravity Energy Storage
abstract: This study evaluates a linear permanent magnet flux switching machine (LPM-FSM) for use in dry gravity energy storage application where electrical energy is stored as potential energy in piston masses. The designed machine is optimized for efficiency and power factor. The optimization is carried out using non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm (NSGA-II). The results indicate that the LPM-FSM has a good power factor and efficiency, which make it a viable option to use as the main drive unit in the linear electric machine gravity energy storage system. The LPM-FSM with multiple sectioned machines, thus with high pole numbers, results in reduced thrust ripple. In comparison to the consequent pole linear vernier hybrid machine, the LPM-FSM provides better performance in terms of power factor and efficiency.

articleTitle: High Torque Density Toroidal Winding Permanent Magnet Vernier Machine with Dual Rotor
abstract: Due to the short end winding length of toroidal windings, it is conducive to improve the torque density of the machine. Therefore, this paper presents a new type of dual-rotor permanent magnet vernier machine with toroidal winding. First, the toroidal winding can effectively reduce the end-winding length, thus reducing the overall machine volume. Meanwhile, the characteristics of high magnetic field modulation ratio is maintained. Second, the incorporation of dual rotor and toroidal winding effectively improves the utilization of armature winding and enhances machine torque density. Time-stepping finite element method is used to analyze and compare the electromagnetic performance of the existing and proposed machines, such as no-load back EMF, torque output capacity, overload capacity, etc., to verify the effectiveness of the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Minor Loop Position and Area Measurement of Inductors for DC-DC converter Considering Excitation Process
abstract: Power conversion circuits based on switching operations are used in automobiles and home appliances to achieve higher efficiency and its miniaturization. Power conversion circuits require the use of inductors, which are characterized by the fact that DC current is superimposed on them. In this circuit, evaluating losses while assuming the actual operating environment has become an issue in the design of inductors. This paper proposes a measurement procedures of minor loop due to differences in the excitation process of inductors used in actual power conversion circuits.

articleTitle: Entropy Change and the Magnetocaloric Effect in R2Cu2X (X=Cd, In)
abstract: In this work, we theoretically discuss the entropy change and the magnetocaloric effect in the compounds <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Gd_{2}Cu_{2}X, Er_{2}Cu_{2}X$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Tm_{2}Cu_{2}X (X= Cd, In)$</tex> by using a model Hamiltonian with two magnetic sub-lattices. In the model, the interactions of the magnetic moments were analyzed within the framework of the mean field theory. Our theoretically calculated magnetocaloric quantities are in reasonable agreement with the experimental data available in the literature.

articleTitle: A Novel Planar Magnetic Flux Concentrator and Its Application in Wireless Power Transfer
abstract: This paper presents a planar magnetic flux concentrator (MFC) to reduce the leakage flux and increase the power transmission in the wireless power transfer (WPT) system. The magnetic field distribution in WPT and eddy current distribution in MFC are investigated. The Finite Element Method (FEM) based simulation results show that the magnetic flux density is increased around the centre hole area of the Tx and Rx coils and decreased in the outer area of the Tx and Rx coils. The experiment results demonstrate that the power transfer can be increased using a planar MFC in the WPT system. The equivalent circuits of WPT transformers with and without a planar MFC are also proposed based on the impedance measurement and analysis. The developed equivalent circuits for the Tx and Rx coils of WPT with MFC are proposed based on the impedance analysis.

articleTitle: Rotor Auxiliary Slot Design Optimization for Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine for Electric Vehicle
abstract: The interior permanent magnet synchronous machine (IPM) with a double-layer permanent magnet (PM) rotor structure is a good candidate machine for electric vehicle drive systems due to its high torque ability and efficiency, however, it also has the disadvantages of high cogging torque and high vibration noise. Improving the air gap flux density distribution is an effective way to reduce the cogging torque and vibration of the electrical machine, which can be achieved by designing the rotor surface with auxiliary slots. The torque performance and vibration of the IPM can be affected by the shape, position, and number of auxiliary slots on the rotor surface. In this paper, the rotor auxiliary slot structure of double V-shaped permanent magnet IPM(D-V IPM) is optimized with cogging torque and air gap electromagnetic density as the optimization objectives, then the influence of the rotor auxiliary slot on the torque performance and vibration of D-V IPM are summarized. A multi-objective genetic algorithm(MOGA) was used to optimize the design of the D-V IPM with four curved auxiliary slots(F-CAS), and the motor performance was verified by experiments.

articleTitle: An Evolutionary Computation Approach for the Electromagnetic Field Assessment of Eddy Current Motion Dampers
abstract: Electromagnetic suspension and damper systems have recently emerged as valid alternatives to the traditionally utilized hydraulic systems. In the past, different analysis approaches were introduced for the performance assessment of active eddy current dampers and shock absorbers. This paper is to present an evolutionary approach for the solution of electromagnetic field problems related to permanent magnet eddy current dampers. The particle swarm optimization, which exploits simple analogues of social interactions, is utilized in the assessment of the permanent magnet eddy current damper forces. Details of the proposed approach and its numerical implementation are given in the paper. The obtained simulation results demonstrate the simplicity and computational efficiency of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Clarification of the Mechanism of Induction Thermography for Crack Detection and Depth Sizing
abstract: Induction thermography (IT) and eddy current testing (ECT) are contactless, non-destructive evaluation (NDE) techniques that can be coupled by eddy currents. By combining the synergized effects of both techniques, we can detect a wider variety of defects and improve detection and sizing reliability. We clarified the mechanism of IT in terms of energy transfer through theoretical and numerical analysis and investigated characteristic features to enhance detection and sizing of cracks in ferromagnetic metal works.

articleTitle: Equivalent Magnetic Network Modeling of Grain-Oriented Silicon Steel Sheets Permanent Magnet Linear Synchronous Motors
abstract: The grain-oriented silicon steel sheet is applied to the primary core of the permanent magnet linear synchronous motor to enhance its thrust density. To compute the performance of the grain-oriented silicon steel sheets permanent magnet linear synchronous motor accurately and rapidly, an equivalent magnetic network model considering the anisotropy of grain-oriented silicon steel sheets is proposed, the uneven magnetic density distribution of the primary tooth and the end effect are also considered. The equivalent magnetic network makes it possible to evaluate the influence of core saturation by iteration, from which the tooth flux density distribution, the flux linkage, the back electromotive force and the thrust of the linear motor are calculated. Finally, the accuracy of the equivalent magnetic network model is verified by the finite element method results.

articleTitle: Investigation on Inclination Angle of Inserted Permanent Magnets in Double-Stator Vernier Machines
abstract: The permanent-magnet (PM) arrangement possesses great influence on the machine performances. In this paper, focusing on the double-stator (DS) inserted-PM (IPM) vernier machines, the effects of the IPM inclination angle are specifically investigated. The variation of the PM inclination angle directly changes the machine flux concentration status, and thus affects the electromagnetic performances. Based on the comparative study of representative machine topologies with PM inclination variation, theoretical conclusions are obtained on the cooperation principle between the PM inclination angle and double stators, and the optimal PM inclination angle for DS-PM vernier machines is obtained.

articleTitle: Effects of the External Vibrations on Rotational Stability of the HTS Magnetic Bearings
abstract: The rotational characteristics of the HTS magnetic bearing system under influence of the external vibrations are studied. The rotational characteristics with and without external vibration is shown. This HTS magnetic bearing system is applied on the superconducting flywheel system for power storage installed on moving and vibrating object such as a vehicle. The HTS magnetic bearing system consists of the rotor with permanent magnet and stator with the HTS. The rotor levitates stably by the pinning effect of the HTS. The flux distribution of the rotor has a large influence on levitation stability. The yoke-equipped cylinder-type rotor is used in this study. The flux from the top of the permanent magnet is interlinked with the HTS by equipping the yoke. This increases the flux use rate of the permanent magnet, and the stability of the rotor is increased. In this study, the stability of the rotating rotor under the influence vibration is evaluated. The influence of vertical oscillation is considered to be small because its amplitude is smaller than that of lateral oscillation. Therefore, only lateral oscillation was measured in this study. The rotor was affected by the vibration, the amplitude increased and the resonance frequency also variated, but levitation kept. However, there was little difference in rotational attenuation after vibration. Therefore, the rotor is affected in the range of vibration, but after the vibration, the rotor levitates stably.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Thermoelectric Ribbon-Shaped Fe3Al Alloys with Large Anomalous Nernst Effect
abstract: Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Al alloys were fabricated into a ribbon shape using a planar flow casting method. Ribbon-shaped Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Al alloys were annealed in an argon atmosphere to improve the anomalous Nernst effect. After annealing at 573–1173 K, the anomalous Nernst coefficient reached 3.2 (or more) µV/K, which is close to that of previously reported Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Al polycrystals (4.0 µV/K). Ribbon-shaped Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Al alloys exhibited sufficient toughness and could be wrapped around a pipe-shaped heat source.

articleTitle: Comparison of Simulation Methods for Angular Dependency When Modeling Demagnetization
abstract: Rare earth element free magnets, such as ferrites, are weaker than their more common alternatives and therefore more prone to demagnetization. Additionally, in permanent magnet electrical machines they are commonly tangentially magnetized and placed in a spoke-type geometry to enhance the magnetic field. In this geometry, the magnets are subject to inclined fields, which are normally not accounted for when evaluating demagnetization risk. In this paper, different methods for demagnetization of permanent magnets are applied to two motors under two distinct loading conditions and the results are compared. It is concluded that it is more important to consider inclined fields when studying ferrite magnets than rare earth element magnets. The common, simplified method of omitting inclined fields is shown to be the most conservative method for evaluating demagnetization. However, more precise results can be reached with methods taking inclined fields into account, especially if the models are adapted for the specific magnet type. Two motors with similar performance have been designed, one with rare earth element magnets and one with ferrites. The motor with ferrites is more sensitive to demagnetization and the bulk of the magnet reaches the demagnetization limit at a lower current than for the motor with rare earth element-based magnets. Finally, demagnetization of magnets is compared for two different rotor positions, emphasizing the importance of considering rotor position when evaluating demagnetization risk.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Wound Laminated Cores for a Dual-Axial Gap Induction Motor Under PWM Excitation
abstract: In recent years, the demand for advanced electric motors has increased as researchers aim to improve the performance of robots and mobile equipment. Therefore, we have developed a high-speed, high-efficiency, three-phase eight-pole dual-axial gap induction motor. Because this new motor is driven using a pulse width modulation (PWM) power supply that operates at high modulation and carrier frequencies, stator cores and rotor cores that offer particularly low eddy current losses are required. To reduce the eddy current losses, we have developed a new wound laminated core structure for this motor by winding a 0.08-mm-thick ultra-thin electrical steel strip. The proposed new core is called a “wound laminated core”. This wound laminated core demonstrated extremely low eddy current losses at high frequencies and harmonics under both sinusoidal wave excitation and PWM excitation. Therefore, this wound laminated core represents an excellent stator core material structure for use in high-speed, high-efficiency motors.

articleTitle: Connected-Skyrmions-Based Racetrack Memory
abstract: Magnetic skyrmions are used as binary digits of a domain motion-type magnetic memory such as racetrack memory. When two or more skyrmions are aligned on a track, a space must exist between each skyrmion. Eliminating this space would increase the storage density of racetrack memory. Thus, this study proposed the use of connected skyrmions as binary digits in racetrack memory and novel domain structures to remove this space. We proposed bi-skyrmion, i.e., two connected skyrmions, and tri-skyrmions, i.e., three connected skyrmions, having skyrmion numbers of 2 and 3, respectively. The connected skyrmions do not have a space between them. We investigate 2-, 3-, and 100-connected skyrmions produced in the nanowire, which is perpendicularly magnetized, using the micromagnetic simulation. The 2-, 3-, and 100-connected skyrmions can be stabilized in the wire. They were moved by the spin-polarized current in a manner similar to the skyrmion.

articleTitle: An MRI-Conditional Implantable Magnet Design with Self-Realigning Orientation
abstract: Patients with “MR Unsafe” rating magnetic implants are required to undergo implant removal surgery before they can take an MRI scan. Only implants labeled as “MR Conditional” can stay in the patient's body for MRI scan under specific conditions. In this article, the authors propose an MRI-conditional implantable magnet design with orientation that can be self-realigned or with an external homing magnet. This design can be readily adopted to a wide range of magnetic implant medical devices on the market, upgrading them from “MR Unsafe” to “MR Conditional” rating. Prototypes are tested to verify the design. Magnetic orientation realignment effectiveness is evaluated.

articleTitle: Direct Magnetic Field Compensation Circuit for Improved Stability of Magnetic Nanoparticle Tomography
abstract: Magnetic nanoparticle tomography (MNT) is an imaging technique that uses magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs). When acquiring signals from MNPs, the detection coil is affected by the magnetic field that excites the MNPs. In the conventional method, a digital-to-analog converter and a voltage divider circuit are used to remove the fundamental signal from the excitation magnetic field. In this study, we propose a circuit that uses a fundamental wave extraction circuit to remove the fundamental wave signal and reduce the influence of direct magnetic field fluctuations. The proposed circuit reduces the influence of direct magnetic field fluctuation and successfully detects a signal of the MNP sample at a depth of 50 mm, confirming the feasibility of MNT.

articleTitle: Effect of Crystallinity on Magnetic Properties in Manganese-Doped Indium Tin Oxide Films
abstract: Mn-doped indium tin oxide (ITO) films were deposited on single crystalline yttria stabilized zirconia (YSZ) substrates with (111) plane orientation and alkali-free glass substrates by rf magnetron sputtering. The epitaxial relationships between the Mn-doped ITO films and YSZ(111) substrates was confirmed by X-ray diffraction measurements. According to the X-ray rocking curve, the epitaxial Mn-doped ITO film on YSZ(111) substrate indicated the high degree of the crystalline alignment. The epitaxial and polycrystalline Mn-doped ITO films exhibited low resistivity and high transparency. Room-temperature ferromagnetism was observed in both the epitaxial and polycrystalline Mn-doped ITO films. The Curie temperature of these films was estimated to be higher than 400 K. The crystallinity difference between the epitaxial and polycrystalline films has little influence on the magnetic properties of the Mn-doped ITO films. The origin of the room-temperature ferromagnetism was discussed on the basis of the correlation between the magnetization and carrier concentration of the Mn-doped ITO films.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties Evaluation of a Compacted Soft Magnetic Composite Core for Permanent Magnet Claw Pole Machine
abstract: Soft magnetic composite (SMC) cores exhibit different magnetic properties at different mass densities and heating treatments. Meanwhile, further mechanical processing on a compacted SMC core can deteriorate its magnetic properties. Therefore, in the development of electrical machines with SMC cores, using the compacted SMC core is very important. However, the required SMC core for the electrical machine is normally irregular in shape and its magnetic properties are determined by the corresponding manufacturing process. Currently, the measurement of the magnetic properties of SMC cores are generally carried out based on ring, sheet, or cubic samples, and few evaluations of the magnetic properties of compacted SMC cores with irregular shape have been performed. In this paper, a magnetic properties measurement system for the compacted SMC stator claw pole teeth is constructed and the sensor measuring field strength is calibrated. Last, a method is proposed to accurately evaluate the magnetic properties of irregular SMC cores.

articleTitle: Analysis of Eddy Current Testing Signals' Frequency Responses and Conductivity-Invariant Crack Sizing
abstract: The eddy current testing (ECT) signals of a crack change with the crack's geometry and electromagnetic properties. The conductivity of the specimen and the conductivity inside or around the crack are generally unknown but play important roles in ECT responses. The objective of this study is to find characteristics features to determine the depth of cracks independently of the material conductivity and the partial conductivity of the cracks. Theoretical and numerical analysis showed that the amplitudes of the intrinsic impedance signal or the magnetic field density signal vary little with frequency. By identifying nearly conductivity-invariant features in the spectra of magnetic flux density signals and constructing a master curve that correlates the characteristic features with crack depth, we will be able to approximately estimate the depth of a crack by referring to the pre-constructed master curve.

articleTitle: Study on Smoothing Generated Voltage in the Vertical Linear Vibration Generator
abstract: It has been expected to create a sustainable society using renewable energy sources. The method of converting vibration energy to electrical energy is examined. In this study, the vertical linear vibration generator was developed to investigate the basic characteristics. The generation voltage increased with an increase in coil turn <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>. However, it did not follow Faraday's law of induction due to the increased thickness of the coil, resulting in a decrease in the generation voltage. The rectification smoothing circuit is used to analyze the smoothing of the generated voltage. The generated voltage obtained from the vibration energy includes various frequency components. The generated AC voltage and then inputted to a smoothing capacitor for smoothing. From this, the optimal smoothing capacitor is examined. As a result, the ripple of the generated voltage was decreased by up to 64%.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Maximum Energy Product by $\alpha$-Fe Coating on the Side of Rectangular Sm(Fe0.8Co0.2)12 Nanoparticles
abstract: The demagnetization process of exchange-coupled Sm(Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.8</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>/<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex>-Fe nanocomposite magnet particles with a-Fe phase coated on the sides of rectangular Sm(Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.8</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf> nanoparticles and the effect of Fe phase arrangement on their <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(BH)_{\max}$</tex> are systematically investigated from micromagnetics calculations. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(BH)_{\max}$</tex> of the reference model Sm(Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.8</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf> particles without Fe layer was 630 kJ/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. On the other hand, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(BH)_{\max}$</tex> of the nanocomposite magnet particle model, in which the four sides of the hard phase are coated with a soft phase, was found to have the highest <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(BH)_{\max}$</tex> of 678 kJ/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. This result may provide a guideline for designing high-performance magnet particle materials while reducing the use of rare metals.

articleTitle: Development of Sm2Fe17N3 Magnetic Powder Doped with La, W, and Ti
abstract: This study investigates the improvement of the magnetic properties of Sm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> powder doped with La, W, and Ti by suppressing fine powder generation in the dispersion process and inhibiting oxidative degradation. Sm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> magnetic powders was developed with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma_{\mathrm{r}}$</tex> of 154 emu/g, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${}_{\mathrm{i}}H_{\mathrm{c}}$</tex> of 10070 Oe (801.8 kAm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>), and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\mathrm{k}}$</tex> of 5642 Oe (449.2 kAm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>) by increasing the nitrogen concentration to 3.46 % via nitridation at 500°C. The magnetic powder was mixed with nylon-12 and injection-molded to produce a bonded magnet. Therefore, bonded magnets with very high magnetic properties of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B_{\mathrm{r}}$</tex> of 0.93 T, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\text{cj}}$</tex> of 1405 kAm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(BH)_{\max}$</tex> of 170 kJm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta(H_{\text{cj}})$</tex> of −0.34 %°C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> were obtained.

articleTitle: PAC Code Construction for Spin-Torque Transfer Magnetic Random Access Memory
abstract: Spin-torque transfer magnetic random access memory (STT-MRAM) is one potential candidate to replace the dynamic random access memory (DRAM) due to its superior features of nonvolatility, fast read/write speed, and high scalability. The error correction coding methods are applied to improve the reliability of STT-MRAM which is affected by the process variation and thermal fluctuation. In this paper, we investigate, for the first time, the design and optimization of the polarization-adjusted convolutional (PAC) code for the STT-MRAM channel. A crucial problem for the application of PAC codes to the STT-MRAM channel is the optimization of the index set of the non-frozen bits of the PAC codes. Hence, a rate-profile optimization method based on the genetic-algorithm-assisted bit-swapping is proposed. Simulation results show that the PAC code with the optimized rate-profile outperforms both the polar code and the PAC code with existing generic rate-profiles.

Author Keywords: Spin-torque transfer magnetic random access memory (STT-MRAM)

articleTitle: Modeling and Experimental Validation of Voltage Distribution in MFTs with Foil Windings
abstract: In this paper, a voltage distribution model for MFTs with foil windings is presented. The model consisting of an equivalent circuit quantified by FEM aims to compute the effects of harmonics in high <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$dv / dt$</tex> pulses from semiconductor switches. In order to verify the accuracy of the model, a test-bench is manufactured and a comparison of experimental and calculation results are performed. The results of this comparison show good agreement between the model and the test-bench, indicating that the model is practical to compute the effects of high <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$dv / dt$</tex> pulses on MFTs. Next, voltage distributions of MFTs with foil and litz windings are computed using the model to verify the difference. The results show that the foil windings is superior with respect to voltage distribution.

articleTitle: Complex Shaped Magnets for an Efficient Use of Rare Earths in Synchro-Reluctant Machines
abstract: In order to maximize the torque of Permanent Magnet assisted Synchronous Reluctance (PMaSynRel) machines, sintered magnets should ideally exhibit curved shapes. Standard process fails to produce such geometries without large critical material loss during machining. The Powder Injection Molding technique has been assessed in this work as an efficient process for producing complex shaped magnets while minimizing the environmental impacts and improving the recyclability of end-of-life products. A case study suited for the automotive sector is presented.

articleTitle: Influence of Airgaps and Rolling Direction Variation Between Grain-Oriented Steel Sheets on Losses in the Magnetic System
abstract: This paper presents results of investigations of the influence of air gaps in GO steel sheet inserts on magnetic losses. Classical iron loss measurements were performed using a single strip tester to magnetize material samples at 50 Hz and 400 Hz. The samples included air gaps of various thickness and it is found that their presence led to the increase of losses up to 30% depending on their size. The variation of the rolling direction has also been studied and revealed no significative influence on magnetic performances. It is concluded that if GO steel inserts are to be used in a magnetic system of an electrical machine, the sheets must be properly connected to reduce the effect of air gaps to increase the overall performances of the machine, but the rolling direction variation in the magnetic flux path has a minor impact on the performances.

articleTitle: Solidification Characteristics and Microstructure Evolutions of RE2Fe14B (RE=Ce, Y, La) Alloys
abstract: The escalation of PrNd costs presents an opportunity for high-abundant and inexpensive Ce-based magnets since the price of Ce is only one thirtieth of PrNd’ s. The high-abundant Ce-based magnets have attracted extensive attention from both academia and industry. However, the magnetic properties of PrNd-Lean Ce-based magnets are still far from their theoretical values due to a deteriorated microstructure. In this article, the solidification behaviors, phase composition characteristics, and phase transformation temperatures of RE2Fe14B (RE= Ce, Y, La) alloys were studied and compared with those of Nd2Fe14B. The main phase reactions of RE2Fe14B (RE = Ce, Y, La) alloys are summarized. It maybe lay a foundation for the development of high abundant rare earth magnets.

articleTitle: Improvement of Transmission Torque Characteristics of Strain Wave Gear with Magnets
abstract: Lower limb exoskeletons with actuators aid physically challenged individuals in walking. However, these exoskeletons weight more than conventional medical devices such as orthoses and walking frames. In this study, we have proposed a novel, lighter than conventional, strain wave gear for exoskeletons. The proposed gear uses magnets, rather than a mechanical cam. The thin-walled elastic cylinder is deformed by the magnetic force in the gear, and the torque is transmitted by tooth engagement. We have designed strain wave gears with small 4 pole and large 16 pole magnets, and constructed a dynamic analysis method; static magnetic analysis calculates the magnetic force distribution on the elastic cylinder, and multi-flexible body dynamics assesses dynamic behavior. From the analyzed and measured results, the gear with the 16 pole magnets transmits larger torque than that with the 4 pole magnets.

articleTitle: A Study of Stable Levitation Conditions Considering Propulsion of a Carrier in the Magnetically Levitated Conveyance System Using the Linear Stepper Motor
abstract: The magnetically levitated conveyance system has been developed. The purpose of this study is to levitate and thrust with the same system. In the conventional system, the carrier did not levitate stably because of large fluctuations in mutual inductance between the track (primary) part and carrier (secondary) part caused by gap fluctuations of the carrier. In this study, the optimal gap and the primary and secondary current values are obtained. As results of experiments, stable levitation is achieved considering the propulsive motion. The minimum attractive force that the carrier levitates stably is examined. In the previous study, the carrier did not levitate because of pitching. Therefore, the difference in the attractive force to suppress pitching is examined.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Double Layer Coils Linear Motor with Series Magnetic Circuit Structure using for Linear Dynamic Loading Platform
abstract: Linear voice coil motor (VCM) has the advantages of high precision and high dynamic response, which fulfills the requirements of linear dynamic loading platform. In this article, a high thrust double layer series magnetic circuit linear voice coil motor is analyzed and designed. Based on 2-D FEM, the thrust and thrust ripple are optimized. Moreover, the damping force on coil support plate is analyzed and reduced by optimization of material and structure. Finally, a linear VCM prototype with a thrust rating of 2000 N is manufactured and tested, the thrust results have good consistency with FEM results.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of High-$B_{s}$ Fe84.3B6P9Cu0.7 Nanocrystalline Alloy Powder
abstract: In this study, we investigated an Fe-B-P-Cu system nanocrystalline alloy with both high saturation magnetic flux density and low coercivity. In particular, we manufactured as-quenched Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">84.3</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</inf>Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.7</inf> alloy powder with a smooth and spherical surface. After annealing, this powder showed a nanocrystalline structure, low coercivity, and saturation magnetic flux density of 1.68 T. These magnetic properties are excellent compared to those of conventional powders. Thus, Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">84.3</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</inf>Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.7</inf> nanocrystalline alloy powder can be used to produce superior inductors with high saturation magnetic flux density as well as low coercivity.

articleTitle: Structure, Magnetism and Electrical Transport of Electron Doped SrCo0.5Nb0.5O3
abstract: A-site nominal doping of disordered perovskite SrCo<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> with La<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>, Nd<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> showed a shift in transition temperature to lower temperatures. Sr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.9</inf>A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.1</inf>(CoNb)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> (A=La, Nd) forms in the tetragonal structure with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I4/m$</tex> symmetry. An increase in unit cell dimensions for La doped sample is observed. Whereas, the Nd doped samples show a decrease in unit cell volume. Electron doping introduces 2+ oxidation state for Co ions, with the Co<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> state still present in the system. Competing ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic interactions are present in the samples, with a rise in antiferromagnetic nature of magnetism exhibited by doped samples. The samples are highly insulating, with the Sr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.9</inf>Nd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.1</inf>(CoNb)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> showing highest resistivity. The high resistivity in the doped samples is consistent with the increase in antiferromagnetic interactions in those.

articleTitle: Measurement and Modelling of Hysteresis Curves for Nonlinear Permanent Magnets at Different Inclination Angles
abstract: This paper presents the measurement results of the BH/MH curves of the Alnico 8 (LNGT40) with recoil loops and a mathematical model for the calculation of the average magnetic flux density in a cubic permanent magnet. The measurements were performed with a Vibrating Sample Magnetometer (VSM). The magnet samples have a cubic shape with 3 mm sides. BH curves in preferred (easy) and transverse directions and recoil loops were measured and compared to Alnico 9 (LNGT72) as well as to the data from the supplier. The load line of the cubic magnet in 0 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A/m$</tex> applied magnetic field was found. A mathematical model was developed which can approximate the MH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf> curve for an applied field with an arbitrarily chosen angle between the field and easy axis, given MH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf> curves for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0^{o}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$90^{o}$</tex>. Also, a simplified general model of a cubic permanent magnet in the air and calculation results of stored energy and hysteresis losses were presented.

articleTitle: Influence of Additional Air Gaps Between Stator Tooth and Back-Iron on Acoustic Performance of Spoke-Type Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
abstract: In this paper, the influence of additional air gaps between stator tooth and back-iron on the acoustic performance of spoke-type permanent magnet synchronous motor (STPMSM) is studied. It is found that the existence of these gaps can reduce the electromagnetic vibration noise, and its sound pressure level decreases by 2.3dB. By comparing radial electromagnetic forces acting on the stator, it is found that the additional air gap will weaken the 2-order radial electromagnetic force in space, which leads to the reduction of electromagnetic vibration noise. In order to further consider the influence of non-uniform additional air gap, the electromagnetic force is decomposed by two-dimensional fast Fourier transform (2D-FFT). The results of space-time spectrum show that the non-uniform air gap will introduce new space-time components of electromagnetic force, but it will not have a great impact on the acoustic performance of STPMSM. In addition, several commonly used stator tooth segments and back-iron segments are compared, which have different shapes of additional air gaps. The results show that the structure with triangular separated stator tooth and back-iron has better acoustic performance.

articleTitle: FeNi-Based Nanocomposite Soft Magnetic Alloy Magnetic and Mechanical Property Tailoring Through Flash Annealing
abstract: Tailoring details of thermal processing, including controlled heating rates and annealing time, plays a key role in enhancement of soft magnetic properties of amorphous and nanocrystalline soft magnetic materials. In particular, rapid thermal processing also known as flash annealing has potential for grain size refinement, tailoring phase identity, and tuning magnetic properties. This work explores the differences between conventional furnace annealing and isothermal annealing with flash annealing techniques for a range of detailed thermal processing conditions (temperature, time, cooling method) in an FeNi-based alloy. As compared to conventional annealing, flash annealing results in dominant FCC <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex> FeNi phase with refined grains. Microstructural refinement due to optimized flash annealing showed improved soft magnetic properties with reduced coercivity and improved ductility for improved core manufacturing at scale.

articleTitle: Simplified Magnetic Flux Density Measurement for Local Resolution Analysis of Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation
abstract: The detailed energy dynamics of transcranial magnetic stimulation of the cerebral cortex remain unclear. The present study therefore examined the energy distribution of transcranial magnetic stimulation. Magnetic energy was assessed using the magnetic flux density, and the locality of transcranial magnetic stimulation was estimated. The magnetic flux density measuring device comprised a pickup probe and simple electronic circuits (e.g., an integrator and buffer amplifier). The pickup probe comprised a sensor coil (with an inner diameter of 8 mm), twisted pair line, and lead-out cable. Magnetic stimulation was applied using a Rapid2 stimulator and a figure-eight flat coil (with a diameter of 70 mm). A simple brain model made from an acrylic plate was based on a subject with a 62%-63% motor threshold and a scalp-to-primary motor cortex distance (i.e., distance from the scalp to the center of the sensor coil) of 15 mm. The highest magnetic flux density after the removal of background noise was approximately 180 mT at the center of the stimulus coil, whereas the resolution of the transcranial magnetic stimulation was approximately 6 mm (i.e., from the center to within ±3 mm). The stimulation area estimated from the measurements was 12 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> around the location of highest magnetic flux density. With the magnetic flux density estimated at the center of the stimulation coil, the stimulus area in which the magnetic flux density decreased by less than 1% was approximately 50.27 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and that in which the magnetic flux density decreased by less than 5% was 254.47 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, It is suggested that the transcranial magnetic stimulation of the cerebral cortex affects areas around the target cerebral cortex. This study showed that the distribution of the magnetic stimulation energy supplied to the target cortex may be evaluated using a simple measurement device and brain model.

articleTitle: Shape Observation by Local illumination Using Reflected Light from Magnetically Controlled Guanine Crystal Platelet
abstract: Biogenic guanine crystal platelets act as micromirror with high reflectivity because the refractive index is 1.83. A strong diamagnetic anisotropy enables the guanine crystals floating in water to control the reflected light direction by a magnetic field of several hundred millitesla. In this paper, we demonstrate the shape observation by reflecting the light, which enters from the side of the specimen to avoid the incident light into a microscope directly, on the broadest surface of guanine crystal platelet just below the specimen. Reflected light illuminates the specimen locally from an oblique direction by adjusting the permanent magnet position. In this case, higher contrast image like dark-field illumination is observed compared to bright-field illumination. In order to improve the controllability of the reflected light angle, the guanine crystal platelets combined with various magnetic nanoparticles are examined to reduce the magnetic field amplitude required for the orientation. The guanine crystals with nanoparticles exhibiting low magnetic field orientation and high reflectivity are obtained for Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> with average particle size of 15 nm. As a result, both the guanine crystal platelet orientation by a three axis Helmholtz coil and high-contrast image observation comparable to that for the guanine crystal without nanoparticle case are successfully achieved.

articleTitle: Semi-Lumped Model for U- and E-Cores for Calculating the Frequency-Dependent Complex Permeance
abstract: Ferrite material has non-negligible permeability, permittivity, and conductivity, so that the magnetic behaviour of ferrite cores is frequency dependent. This article presents a method to predict the complex permeance of ferrite E- and U-cores including electromagnetic resonance. The cores are decomposed into elementary segments, for which the Maxwell equations are solved analytically to obtain a network of frequency-dependent permeances or reluctances.

articleTitle: Biocompatible Nanoparticles for Drug-Delivery System with Field-Dependent Radical Pair System
abstract: In this paper, we used 2,2’-azobis(isobutyronitrile) (AIBN) as a radical pair-forming agent to investigate whether magnetic fields can control a liposomal drug release through differences in the physical properties of biomembranes. Exposure to a static magnetic field of 0.25 T was performed using a pair of commercially available permanent magnets. Irradiations of ß-carotene-containing liposomal nanocarriers modified with AIBN were performed using an original air-cooled UV -LED irradiation system. Under exposure to the static field, the AIBN in the membrane was excited by a UV -LED emission wavelength of 365 nm. According to the overall result of seven kinds of prepared nanocarriers, the drug release potentials with magnetic field effects obtained using a static field of 0.25 T were more extensive on the order of 16-32%, than those obtained at geomagnetic fields. Conclusively, we strongly propose a novel photomagnetic controlled drug-release technology using these liposomal nanocarriers equipped with magnetic controls.

articleTitle: An Extremely Low Frequency Magnetic Control Study of Metamorphic Qualities in Thyroxine-Administrated Axolotls (Ambystoma mexicanum)
abstract: With a full understanding of a commercialized power frequency of 50/60 Hz, considerations for details in the competing situation between extremely low frequency (ELF)-field effects and biological adaptive responses to the magnetic forces in a living body are of great importance. The purpose of this paper is to investigate ELF magnetic effects with different exposure timings on the forced metamorphosis of Mexican axolotls, which is induced by a function of thyroxine (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>). One hundred and forty axolotls (about 5 months old, approximately 80 mm) were individually kept in appropriate square boxes containing a dechlorinated water without aeration. Following a soak with T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> for 60 h, the T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> solution was displaced by a dechlorinated water, employing an original water-renewing system. Exposures of T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>-administrated axolotls to ELF fields (5.0 mT at 10 Hz) were performed using an air-cored coil system. The water temperature was strictly controlled at 24°C. The morphological changes and the survival rates of the axolotls affected by the prestimulation of the T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> were monitored every day. In consequence, we discovered that the initiation timings of ELF field exposure did influence the speed of the morphological changes, as well as the survival rates of the following salamanded axolotls. As a point worthy of special mention, there was a close connection between the T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>-corresponding survival rates and serious indigestion/anorexia in the salamanded bodies. Our data could prove to be helpful for future reference with respect to a magnetic control study of tissue-regeneration.

articleTitle: Effects of Partial Non-Magnetic Improvement Length and Position in the Bridge on the Flux of a Rotor Core for Obtaining a High Magnetic Flux
abstract: The present study investigates the impact of a non-magnetic improvement treatment on the bridge of the rotor core sheet, with an emphasis on the effects of the length and position of the treatment on magnetic properties. A prototype rotor core was fabricated by laminating 60 rotor core sheets. The effect of the non-magnetic improvement length on the magnetic flux at the relative improved position of 0% was evaluated, and the rotor core improved with an improvment ratio of 70%, showing a 38.0% magnetic flux increment. The effect of the relative improvement position on the magngetic flux with the improvement ratio of 70%-76 % was evaluated. Findings demonstrate that the rotor core with a relative improvement position of −27% exhibits a significant magnetic flux increment of 40.1%.

articleTitle: Microstructure and Magnetic Characterization on Ball-Milled Fe-Based Nanocrystalline Alloy Sheet
abstract: In this work, ball-milled iron (Fe)-based nanocrystalline alloy sheets and obtaining platelet particles are used to effectively utilize the end material and apply it to a soft magnetic composite. The instrumental analysis results reveal that, although a microstrain is introduced into the nanocrystalline α-Fe grains in the achieved alloy powder, the amorphous part filled among the grains experiences almost no change. The ball-milling treatment greatly increases the coercive force of the pulverized nanocrystalline sheet. Although the coercive force of the alloy powder decreases after the heat treatment, it remained approximately 10 times higher than that of the heat-treated alloy sheet without the ball-milling treatment, even after the heat treatment. The magnetic process of the ball-milled and post-annealed nanocrystalline alloy powder is discussed based on the results of the synchrotron radiation X-ray analysis and transmission electron microscopy with the Lorentz technique.

articleTitle: Dual-Electrodynamic Wheel Force Analysis
abstract: The rotation of an electrodynamic wheel (EDW) above a flat conductive, non-magnetic, track induces currents in the track that can create lift and thrust/braking force. This paper presents a new type of dual-EDW that consists of two EDWs in series that can also create a controllable lateral force. The magnitude and direction of the lateral force can be changed via the relative phase angle shifting of the two rotors. The changes in the lateral force magnitude as well as direction are shown to not affect the lift and thrust force magnitude. The geometric analysis of the design is presented and the practical difficulty of implementing the design is also discussed.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Conduction Property to Improve Performance of Conductive Shield Layer Installed in Magnetically Shielded Rooms
abstract: To improve the shielding performance of magnetically shielded rooms (MSRs) used in biomagnetism measurements and to ensure their stability, we evaluated the electrical conduction properties at contact parts of conductor plates. These conductor plates are used as the conductive shield layer and form an integral part of the MSRs along with the magnetic shield layer. Although the conductive shield layer prevents magnetic noises with wide frequencies using the eddy current effect, poor electrical contact between the conductor plates causes increased electric resistance at that particular part. Consequently, this diminishes the effectiveness of the eddy current, thus lowering the shielding performance of the conductive shield layer. Therefore, cases of poor electrical contact should be detected and rectified to ensure high shielding performance and maintain stability. In this study, we develop resistance sensors to detect areas of poor contact. By establishing a quantitative relationship between poor contact and shielding performance, we can better understand the significance of these processes in improving and maintaining optimal performance. Moreover, we describe an application example of these resistance sensors on an actual construction site of an MSR.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Noise Suppression Sheet Embedded in Printed Circuit Boards
abstract: To address potential electromagnetic interference (EMI) issues in highly dense electronic circuits, where electric components and interconnections are integrated in proximity, we investigated the effectiveness of integrating a noise suppression sheet (NSS) inside printed circuit boards (PCBs). We fabricated NSSs compatible with PCB embedding and systematically evaluated their noise suppression performance. Using a newly proposed measurement jig to simulate the embedding of NSSs in PCBs, we confirmed the suppression effect of conduction and radiation noise. We also embedded NSSs in PCBs used in actual products and confirmed the validity of PCB-integrated NSS for suppressing radiation noise in the frequency range of 700MHz to 1GHz, which is widely used for telecommunications.

articleTitle: Microwave Absorption Properties of Fe/Fe16N2 Nanoparticles Prepared from Iron Oxide
abstract: Fe/Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanoparticles were synthesized from Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> nanoparticles by hydrogen reduction and subsequent low-temperature nitridation. XRD analysis revealed that the Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> phase was fully transformed into the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex>-Fe phase after hydrogen reduction at 400°C. The Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> phase was observed after ammonia nitridation of the Fe nanoparticles at temperatures ranging from 140°C to 160°C. The weight fraction of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> increased with increasing nitridation temperature, leading to enhanced coercivity. Evaluation of the electromagnetic properties of resin composites of the samples revealed a resonance frequency of 6.9 GHz for the reduced Fe nanoparticles, which shifted to 9.5 GHz after nitridation owing to the large anisotropic field of the Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> crystal structure. The obtained results suggest that resin composites containing Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanoparticles are promising microwave absorption materials for 5G applications.

articleTitle: Model for Angular Dependency of the Intrinsic Coercivity of Ferrite Permanent Magnets
abstract: In internal permanent magnet synchronous machines (IPMSM), the use of ferrite permanent magnets is being studied as an alternative to rare-earth elements-based permanent magnets, such as NdFeB. However, demagnetization measurements of ferrite magnets are rarely published and such information is crucial for an efficient electrical machine design with ferrite magnets. In this paper, we present measurements of partial demagnetization on ferrite permanent magnets subject to inclined external magnetic fields. From the measurements done, mathematical models are developed for Y30 and Y40 samples that defines a relationship between the intrinsic coercivity and the inclination of the external demagnetizing field. Furthermore, from the primary results, the angular dependency of hysteresis losses and relative permeability are also explored, as well as their impact on the design of IPMSM.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Performance Analysis Method of the Variable Gear Ratio Magnetic Gear
abstract: This paper investigates the dynamic characteristics of a variable gear ratio magnetic gear (VGRMG) by using a dynamic performance analysis method proposed, which is based on the torque look-up table model of the VGRMG obtained by the finite element method (FEM) with correction. The gear ratio regulation and dynamic characteristics are tested on the prototype and test bench of the VGRMG. It is found that the measured gear ratios match the theoretical values well, the maximum relative error is about 0.41%. The speed curves of the two rotors and torque curves obtained by the dynamic performance experiment also match the simulation results well, except for a large overshoot caused by a transient 38Nm load torque produced by the inner rotor driving induction motor which is not considered in the simulation. The experimental results verify the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed dynamic performance analysis method.

articleTitle: Surrogate-Based Modeling of Induction Machines to Reduce the Computational Burden of Robust Multi-Objective Optimization
abstract: One of the main obstacles to robust design optimization of Induction Machines (IM) is the high computational burden, which is mainly due to time-intensive nonlinear finite element (FE) simulations. The large multivariable design space of electric machine optimization typically requires running thousands of simulations taking many hours, if not days which is quite prohibitive. To overcome this bottleneck, hybridization of FE-based optimization with approximate models can lead to expedite the process. This paper is focused on accelerating the typical FE-based optimization scenarios by implementing and systematically studying an ensemble of surrogate models of IMs in terms of computational burden and performance. In this regard, after adopting the most significant surrogate model, a multi-points sequential sampling process with a two-step surrogate-based optimization approach is developed. Compared with direct FE-based robust optimization, competitive results are achieved by adopting the proposed hybrid surrogate-based approach and the overall runtime is reduced by 69%. Furthermore, as a case study, an optimization problem for an 11-kW IM is considered by applying the typical FE-based optimization task followed by the proposed hybrid technique. Hence, the achievable speed improvements, as well as further possible enhancing means are discussed. The detailed comparison of the presented surrogate models makes a comprehensive source for engineers and designers to follow.

articleTitle: An Integrated Axial-Flux Magnetic-Geared Double-Rotor Machine Using Harmonic Current Injection Method for HEVs
abstract: Enjoying the merits of compact structure, less noise and high specific power, axial-flux magnetic-geared double-rotor machines (AMGDRMs) have been proved a promising candidate for the electrical-continuously variable transmission (e-CVT) in hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs). However, an additional permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) is needed for torque compensation in the e-CVT system. In this paper, a novel integrated scheme which can realize the functional integration of a PMSM is proposed to improve compactness further. By carefully designing pole-pair number combination, the PMSM torque would be produced by the interaction between the armature fifth-harmonic and PM fundamental magnetic fields when injecting harmonic current. However, such combination would cause significant principled torque ripple. Hence, a suppression method based on the phase-shift structure is proposed to cancel the torque fluctuation out, thus the proposed machine can enable both the MGDRM and PMSM operations without significant torque ripple. Compared with existing dual-winding integrated schemes, an integrated winding configuration where only one set of conventional integral-slot winding is placed into one stator is adopted in the proposed machine, simplifying the manufacture process. First, the machine structure and operation principle are investigated. Second, the torque ripple suppression mechanism is analyzed. Finally, 3-D FEA simulations are carried out to validate the proposed machine and evaluate overall performances.

articleTitle: Understanding the Coercivity of Ga-Containing Nd-Fe-B Sintered Magnets from Feature Extraction and Selection of X-Ray Diffraction Patterns via Dimension Reduction and Sparse Modeling
abstract: Coercivity enhancement of Ga-containing Nd-Fe-B as-sintered magnets driven by the microstructural changes occurring during post-sinter annealing was studied via feature extraction and selection based on several data science methods. These data science methods reveal the correlation between the coercivity and the intensity and shape change of the specific structures in the X-ray diffraction pattern. Principal component analysis, a linear model with least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, and nonlinear random forest regression modeling of coercivity based on X-ray diffraction patterns objectively identified the microstructural changes correlating with coercivity enhancement. Further, quantitative evaluation of the correlation magnitude of microstructural changes to the coercivity of the magnet revealed a preferred direction of the correlation magnitude even in an identical phase. The validity of our findings was qualitatively confirmed based on the results of previous studies, indicating that sparse modeling accelerates materials research and development via automated decision-making.

articleTitle: The International Magnetics Conference (INTERMAG) 2023 Foreword
abstract: Over 1500 magnetism researchers journeyed to beautiful Sendai Japan the week of May 15-19, 2023 for the IEEE International Magnetics Conference (INTERMAG 2023), which was co-sponsored by IEEE and the Magnetism Society of Japan (MSJ). These in-person attendees were later joined by 271 virtual registrants. The self-reported home regions were Asia (74%), Europe (19%), North America (5%), and other parts of the globe (2%).

articleTitle: The International Magnetics Conference (INTERMAG) 2023 Preface
abstract: ON BEHALF of the organizing committee, it is our pleasure to present selected papers from the INTERMAG 2023 Conference, which was held in Sendai, Japan, during May 15–19, 2023. The outstanding quality of the conference is reflected by the scientific and technical quality of the papers in this Conference Proceedings. The Publications Committee received 560 manuscripts, which were submitted for peer review and possible publication in either IEEE TRANSACTIONS ON MAGNETICS or this Conference Proceedings. In order to be considered for publication, the manuscripts were required to meet rigorous criteria for novelty in applied and basic magnetism. Following the standard IEEE review process, each paper published in IEEE TRANSACTIONS ON MAGNETICS and in the Conference Proceedings was reviewed by at least two anonymous referees. In the end, 279 papers were accepted for publication in IEEE TRANSACTIONS ON MAGNETICS and 55 papers in this Conference Proceedings.
